text: In the input-driven (skew-product) view, what condition makes a reservoir exhibit generalized synchronization / the echo state property?
choices: All conditional Lyapunov exponents of the driven reservoir are negative, so its state converges to a function of the input history independent of initial conditions
The driver and the reservoir must obey identical equations of motion
The conditional Lyapunov exponents of the reservoir are positive
The reservoir state feeds back and drives the input signal in a two-way coupling
explanation: Generalized synchronization / the ESP holds when all conditional Lyapunov exponents are negative (Pecora-Carroll), so the driven reservoir contracts to a function of the input history and forgets its initial state. GS explicitly does NOT require identical equations (option 1), needs negative not positive exponents (option 2), and the skew-product coupling is one-way driver -> reservoir (option 3).
